atoms.text: This level includes mentions of uncomfortable situations both at school and at home. If this level upsets you, you should speak with a trusted adult about it.

instruction.text: How should you deal with secrets? Fill in the gaps.

feedback.finish: Also remember that you never have to listen to anyone’s secrets if you don’t want to. Having to keep people’s secrets can be tiring or stressful.

atoms.b: You ((++have don’t_have)) the right to keep secrets to yourself, and ((++no_one your_friend)) should put pressure on you to tell them anything.
If your friend has told you a secret, it means they trust you not to tell anyone else. You should ((++respect ignore)) this.
However, in some cases, it would help your friend much more to not keep their ((++secret belongings)). Their secret might be putting them in ((++danger school)).

instruction.text: What are some things you might want to keep secret from people you know? Select all the correct answers.

feedback.finish: These are some secrets that are okay to keep. It’s okay to hide some things about yourself from others! You should also try not to spoil a surprise party or present.

instruction.text: What kinds of secrets should you not keep? Select the three correct answers.

feedback.end: In these cases, you should tell a trusted adult. You might feel like you are breaking your friend’s trust, but keeping them or other people safe is more important.

instruction.text: Should you keep these secrets or tell them to an adult?

hint.text: Think about how serious the situation is. Anything that seriously affects someone’s life should be shared with a trusted adult.

atoms.a: your friend taking an extra cookie
a stranger on the internet asking your friend to meet up
your parents planning a surprise birthday party for your sibling
your friend being hurt at home
your friend regularly stealing from shops
your friend not knowing how to tie their shoelaces
your friend being bullied but not wanting anyone to know

feedback.finish: Some secrets can make you feel worried or upset. In these cases, you should tell your parent or guardian or your teacher. They will do their best to help.
